How recycled bridges and shipwrecks are creating new marine habitats

For decades, parts of Chesapeake Bay have quietly absorbed fragments of American infrastructure that had already lived one life elsewhere. Retired ships, concrete structures and carefully prepared materials have found a second purpose on the seabed, where currents, shellfish and algae gradually transform bare surfaces into living habitat. One of the most striking examples arrived in 2017, when thousands of tonnes of concrete from Virginia's demolished Old Dominion Boulevard Bridge were lowered into the bay as part of an artificial reef programme. The project reflected a broader idea that obsolete structures, if handled correctly, can support marine life rather than simply becoming waste. In the Chesapeake, that thinking has shaped restoration work for years. Artificial reefs like these not only create shelter for fish, crabs and oysters but also help strengthen local fisheries, improve biodiversity and reduce construction waste, demonstrating how carefully planned recycling projects can deliver long-term environmental and economic benefits simultaneously.When the Old Dominion Boulevard Bridge in Virginia Beach was replaced, officials faced the familiar question of what to do with the vast amount of reinforced concrete left behind.Instead of sending everything to landfill, large sections were cleaned, broken into suitable sizes and transported offshore to become part of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel artificial reef system. According to the Virginia Marine Resources Commission, the project placed as much as 20,000 tons of bridge material on the seabed during 2017, expanding an existing reef already used by fish, crabs and other marine species. The concrete was selected because it remains stable underwater and gradually develops rough surfaces that allow barnacles, mussels, oysters and algae to settle. Those early colonisers attract small fish, which in turn draw larger predators into the area.Artificial reefs are designed to imitate some of the shelter provided by natural rocky bottoms, which are relatively uncommon in much of the bay. Rather than creating a single solid structure, the bridge sections were arranged to leave open spaces and varied heights, producing places where marine animals can feed, hide and reproduce.The Chesapeake already offers an example of how abandoned structures can unexpectedly evolve into wildlife habitat. Along Maryland's side of the Potomac River, the remains of the famous Mallows Bay "Ghost Fleet" have spent decades slowly merging with the surrounding landscape after hundreds of obsolete wooden ships were abandoned there during the twentieth century. According to the U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD), the Mallows Bay "Ghost Fleet" originated after the U.S. Shipping Board's World War I wooden shipbuilding programme left hundreds of surplus vessels without a commercial future. Many were sold to Western Marine & Salvage Company in 1922, which attempted to dismantle them before abandoning much of the fleet in Mallows Bay after economic setbacks. Surveys identified dozens of wooden steamships alongside barges, ferries and much older vessels, while also documenting an ecosystem supporting fish, birds, reptiles and extensive aquatic vegetation. That combination of cultural history and ecological value eventually contributed to the area's recognition as a protected marine sanctuary.The bridge reef follows a different path because it was intentionally engineered rather than accidentally created. Yet both places illustrate the same ecological principle: once stable surfaces remain underwater long enough, marine organisms often begin turning them into functioning habitat.Scientists have examined artificial reefs around the world to understand how well they support marine ecosystems. According to the study published in PLOS ONE, titled ‘ A systematic review of artificial reefs as platforms for coral reef research and conservation ’, it found that projects frequently recorded higher fish abundance, expanded habitat and, in some cases, increased coral cover or nursery areas for marine species. Success, however, depended heavily on thoughtful design, clear conservation goals and long-term monitoring rather than simply placing material underwater. The review also points out that artificial reefs work on relatively small scales. They can provide new surfaces for marine life and improve local habitat, but they cannot replace entire natural ecosystems or solve broader environmental pressures such as climate change, pollution or habitat loss. In many cases, researchers found that monitoring periods were too short to judge whether reefs produced lasting ecological gains. That perspective is reflected in projects across Chesapeake Bay. Artificial reefs are viewed as one tool within a wider restoration effort that also includes oyster recovery, water quality improvements and protection of natural wetlands.The idea of recycling large structures into underwater habitat continues to gain attention because it combines waste reduction with environmental restoration. Concrete bridges, prepared ships and other suitable materials can remain stable for decades, offering attachment points for marine organisms and creating shelter where little previously existed.The 2017 bridge project showed how infrastructure nearing the end of its useful life can continue serving a different purpose beneath the water's surface. While the concrete no longer carries traffic across the bay, it now contributes to an evolving underwater landscape that supports fish and other marine life. Like the long-submerged wrecks at Mallows Bay, it demonstrates that, under carefully managed conditions, relics of the past can become part of a living ecosystem rather than disappearing from it altogether.
Article Summary: Artificial reefs are designed to imitate some of the shelter provided by natural rocky bottoms, which are relatively uncommon in much of the bay. Concrete bridges, prepared ships and other materials can remain stable for decades, offering suitable attachment points for oysters, mussels and algae.

Article Title: In 2011, three U.S. states sank a 563-foot Navy destroyer in the Atlantic; Hurricane Irene later broke the new artificial reef into three pieces
Article Text:
In 2011, the Arthur W. Radford, a decommissioned U.S. Navy destroyer, was intentionally sunk to create an artificial reef, promoting marine life and offering divers a unique underwater experience. Following Hurricane Irene, the ship was fragmented into three sections on the ocean floor.

Turning a naval vessel into an ocean landmark

Despite this disintegration, the wreckage remains a crucial habitat for various marine species, exemplifying the adaptability of human constructs to nature's forces. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons

A hurricane reshaped the wreck

A retired U.S. Navy destroyer was expected to begin a new chapter beneath the Atlantic Ocean in 2011. The 563-foot Arthur W. Radford was sunk as part of the Del-Jersey-Land Reef project, a joint effort involving New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland. The aim was to create an offshore site that could support fishing, diving and marine life.The wreck’s condition changed later that month. After the Radford was sunk on August 10, 2011, Hurricane Irene affected the Mid-Atlantic region on August 27–28. The storm passed over the Del-Jersey-Land Reef, and scuba divers who visited the site shortly afterwards documented that the Radford had broken into three pieces.The New Jersey Fish & Wildlife Digest article Radford Reef by Hugh M. Carberry, published in 2012, recorded the journey of the former Spruance-class destroyer from naval vessel to underwater attraction. The article described how the ship underwent extensive preparation before it could be sunk offshore.Preparing the Radford was a detailed process that took about 16 months, according to the article. Workers cleaned the vessel, removed materials that could create environmental concerns and inspected areas of the ship before it was approved for sinking. The New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife report noted that testing and removal efforts were carried out to reduce potential risks from materials such as coatings and other ship components.The destroyer was also modified to make it more suitable for divers. Certain areas were opened, obstacles were removed, and safety improvements were made so divers could move through sections of the vessel more easily. The work was intended to help the ship settle safely into the reef site.On August 10, 2011, the Radford was sunk at the Del-Jersey-Land Reef site in approximately 135 feet of water. The vessel settled upright on the seabed, creating a large structure in an otherwise open stretch of ocean. Its size and design, including multiple decks and rooms, provided surfaces and shelter for marine organisms.Large vessels are often used for reef projects because they offer more complex shapes and surfaces than smaller materials. The report explained that the Radford’s structure created areas where organisms could attach and where fish could find shelter. Over time, these spaces were expected to support the growth of a new underwater community.The Radford’s planned future changed when Hurricane Irene arrived later that month. Strong conditions from the storm affected the recently placed ship, and follow-up dives revealed that the destroyer had separated into three major pieces.Although the vessel was no longer a single intact wreck, the change did not eliminate its value as a reef site. The broken sections created a new layout on the seabed, giving divers new areas to explore and changing how the wreck interacted with its surroundings.The 2012 New Jersey Fish & Wildlife Digest article explained that organisms including hydroids, anemones and blue mussels could gradually settle on the ship’s surfaces. Early observations after deployment also recorded fish around the wreck, including black sea bass.As the site developed, different sections of the wreck offered varied diving experiences depending on depth and conditions. The ship's size and layout meant divers could explore different parts of the former destroyer while observing the early stages of reef development, according to the report.The Radford shows how a planned engineering project can change when it meets natural forces. The vessel was carefully prepared to serve as an offshore habitat, but the ocean ultimately shaped its final form.After Hurricane Irene, the wreck was no longer a single ship but still served the reef project. A destroyer built for military operations became part of an underwater landscape, offering a glimpse of how human-made structures can take on a different role after leaving active service.
Article Summary: Arthur W. Radford, a decommissioned U.S. Navy destroyer, was intentionally sunk to create an artificial reef in 2011. Following Hurricane Irene, the ship was fragmented into three sections on the ocean floor. Despite this disintegration, the wreckage remains a crucial habitat for various marine species.

What began as a quiet bonding exercise between a California singer-songwriter and a rescued horse has evolved into one of the internet's most unusual musical collaborations. Los Angeles-based musician Mikayla Khramov says her rescue horse, Yupia, developed a fascination with musical instruments while she volunteered at a horse rescue in California. Instead of discouraging the curiosity, she nurtured it, eventually teaching Yupia to strum a guitar and pluck a harp using his nose and teeth. After years of viral videos attracting millions of views online, Khramov is now incorporating the horse's unique sounds into an upcoming album, turning an unlikely friendship into a creative musical project.Khramov first met Yupia while volunteering at a horse rescue in California. She noticed that the horse was unusually drawn to music and would often approach her whenever she played an instrument.Rather than using treats or force to encourage the behaviour, she allowed Yupia to explore the instruments at his own pace. Over time, he learned to gently strum guitar strings and pluck the strings of a harp with his nose, lips and teeth. Khramov has described the sessions as a way of building trust and strengthening their bond rather than training the horse to perform.Yupia does not play the guitar or harp in the same way a human musician would. Instead, he produces sounds by naturally interacting with the strings, creating notes and rhythms that are recorded during their sessions.Videos shared by Khramov show the horse independently approaching instruments and making sounds without prompting. These recordings are then combined with professional music production to create finished tracks.The upcoming album will blend Yupia's instrument sounds with Khramov's vocals and songwriting.According to Khramov, the recordings will include guitar and harp sounds created by the horse, along with natural audio such as his whinnies, breathing and hoofbeats. She is also collaborating with musicians from Portugal to produce the final compositions. An EP is expected to follow the album.Khramov says the musical sessions became an important part of Yupia's rehabilitation after his rescue. Instead of relying on conventional training methods, she used music as a calming activity that encouraged curiosity and confidence.She believes the experience demonstrates how patience, trust and positive interaction can help strengthen relationships between humans and animals.Clips of Yupia strumming guitars and playing harps have been circulating on social media for several years, attracting millions of views across platforms.The videos have generated widespread curiosity, with many viewers amazed by the horse's apparent enthusiasm for music. Alongside her music career, she has spent years working with rescued animals and frequently shares stories about the bond between humans and horses.Her collaboration with Yupia has become one of her best-known projects, combining music, storytelling and animal welfare in a way that has resonated with audiences around the world.The album is not intended to present Yupia as a professional musician but as a creative partner whose natural curiosity inspired an entirely new artistic direction. By combining the horse's authentic sounds with original songs, Khramov hopes to celebrate the bond they have built since meeting at a California rescue. The project serves as a reminder that meaningful connections can emerge in unexpected ways, even between a singer and a horse that simply loved the sound of music.

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: AI is in finance, but is it ready? 76% firms use AI as governance lags, says report
Article Text:
Only 28% are reassessing the talent profiles needed for an AI-driven finance workforce.

Better AI needs better data

AI is becoming a bigger part of finance departments, but companies are finding that adopting the technology is easier than figuring out how people, data and controls should work around it.A KPMG report found that 76 per cent of organisations are already using AI in financial planning. Yet the report suggests that simply adding AI tools will not be enough to create an advantage. The bigger gains are expected to come from using AI to support better financial decisions, while building the systems and governance needed to manage its growing role."Competitive advantage will increasingly belong to organizations that align their finance operating model around AI -- and can sustain that alignment as AI becomes more capable, more autonomous and more deeply embedded in everyday decision-making."The shift is also exposing a gap in how companies are preparing their finance teams.While 38 per cent of organisations are upskilling finance and internal audit employees for AI-enabled processes, only 28 per cent are hiring for new skill sets. An identical 28 per cent are reassessing the talent profiles they will need as AI becomes more deeply integrated into finance.In other words, most organisations are teaching their existing workforce to use AI rather than redesigning the workforce around human-AI collaboration.That transition is also keeping humans firmly in the loop. KPMG found that 33 per cent of organisations are increasing human oversight specifically because of concerns linked to AI.This remains particularly important in finance, where decisions can involve regulatory requirements and professional judgement. Human checks, the report said, can make AI-driven outputs more reliable while helping organisations build confidence in the technology.Even as companies expand AI use, the quality of the underlying data remains a major constraint.About 36 per cent of organisations identified better data quality, integration and interoperability between systems as the biggest opportunity to get more value from AI in finance.The challenge, therefore, is not simply having more AI tools. Finance teams also need to understand which data can be trusted, how AI-generated outputs should be interpreted and how those findings can be translated into decisions."Data fluency is emerging as the most critical capability need: the ability to assess data quality, interpret outputs and communicate findings in terms the business can act on."The report's broader takeaway is that AI adoption alone may not determine which finance teams benefit most. Companies that combine the technology with stronger governance, appropriate talent and reliable data are likely to be better placed as AI becomes more autonomous.
Article Summary: KPMG: 76% of organisations are already using AI in financial planning. Only 28% are reassessing the talent profiles needed for an AI-driven finance workforce. Companies that combine the technology with stronger governance, appropriate talent and reliable data will benefit most.

Article Title: Before the knowledge walks out the door
Article Text:
Everyone in Silicon Valley is racing to build machines that replace human expertise.

Ahmer Inam

, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it.

When Ahmer Inam appeared on Fox & Friends in June, his mother watched the segment without following much of it. Her English is limited. There was her son on the famous curved couch of American morning television, fielding questions about artificial intelligence, and she understood almost none of the words. She wept anyway. Some distances need no translation, and the one between a schoolteacher's household in Delhi and a Manhattan television studio is legible in any language.Had she followed the argument, it might have surprised her less than it surprised the audience. Because what Inam was defending, underneath the vocabulary of frontier AI, is approximately the oldest idea in civilisation — the one his father practised for a living: that knowledge survives only when one generation troubles to hand it to the next.Inam has spent twenty-five years building artificial intelligence — long enough to remember when it meant symbolic logic in the late nineties, and senior enough to have run AI and data for Fortune 500 companies, Nike and Wells Fargo among them, back when "chief AI officer" was still an exotic title. He is not, in other words, a critic sniping from the cheap seats. Which makes the thesis of Cognisee, the research lab he founded and leads, sound almost seditious in today's Silicon Valley: "We're not trying to replace the worker," he says."We're trying to make the worker irreplaceable."The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage." By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030 — electricians, welders, machinists, the hands America needs if it is serious about building factories, chip plants and grid capacity again. But Inam's diagnosis is sharper than a headcount. "America does not have a work shortage," he likes to say. "It has an expertise shortage."Consider what actually leaves the building when a master electrician retires at sixty-eight. Not the manual — the manual stays. What leaves is the ear that catches a motor running slightly wrong two weeks before it fails; the instinct that connects a faint vibration to a pattern in old maintenance logs; forty years of judgment that was never written down because it could not be. The philosopher Michael Polanyi had a name for this — tacit knowledge, the things we know but cannot tell — and Cognisee is, at bottom, a bet that the most valuable training data on earth is tacit.The company's method has a fable-like symmetry. Its AI begins as an apprentice: it works alongside experienced people and learns what they notice, what they ask, how they make judgment calls. Then it turns around and becomes a coach, carrying that accumulated judgment to the newcomer. "First it's an apprentice," Inam says. "Then it becomes a coach." Picture a 22-year-old on his first aircraft-maintenance job, hearing a sound he has never heard before, with the distilled instincts of the country's best technicians beside him in real time. "He's not being replaced by a machine," Inam says. "He's being mentored by one."The repository where all this lives is called, a little grandly, a Wisdom Vault — a secure library of hard-won know-how from doctors, nurses, electricians, factory workers, farmers, small-business owners. Grand or not, the name gives away the emotional register Inam is working in. This is not pitched as workforce optimisation. It is pitched as inheritance.He is careful — insistent, actually — about the question that framing invites: who owns it? In Cognisee's design, the expert decides what to preserve, what to share, and with whom; the contributor is recognised and rewarded; the knowledge belongs to the person who earned it, not to the machine that absorbed it. "There is a big difference," Inam says, "between being monitored and being mentored." The company is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which he describes as a legal commitment to the worker rather than a marketing pledge.That ownership principle is also where his quarrel with the reigning AI paradigm becomes explicit. The frontier labs, Inam argues, got intelligent by swallowing the written internet — and the written internet is now substantially swallowed, which is why the industry's plan increasingly amounts to bigger data centres and more electricity, even as some of the field's own pioneers warn of a wall ahead. His contrarian wager is that the next leap will come not from more compute but from the knowledge that never made it onto the internet in the first place — and that it can be gathered by consent rather than by crawler.For an Indian reader, the resonance is hard to miss. This is a country that has watched its weaves, its remedies and its craft knowledge catalogued, carried off and sold back to it before. It is also a country whose deepest teaching traditions were never textual at all, but moved from person to person — the guru-shishya parampara, the ustad and the shagird. Inam has spoken about Wisdom Vaults for indigenous and medicinal knowledge, with communities retaining ownership of what they contribute. One way to describe Cognisee is as an attempt to give the world's oral inheritances an infrastructure layer — sovereignty included.The idea is attracting converts from unexpected quarters. Cognisee's co-founder, Alex Giannou, spent nearly two decades on Wall Street financing precisely the data centres and power deals behind the AI boom; he crossed over, in Inam's telling, because the right bet and the smart bet turned out to be the same one. Among the company's early backers is a senior Google executive who helped invent federated learning, one of the foundational privacy-preserving techniques of modern machine learning. And last year the XPRIZE Foundation, where Inam serves as a Visionary, recognised his work with its Global Visioneering Award.None of which quite explains the conviction. For that you have to go back to Delhi. Inam grew up in a low-income household, the son of a teacher — a man who spent his working life on the least scalable expertise-transfer technology ever devised: one adult, one room, one generation at a time. The son's journey to America was not gilded; there were stretches, early on, when he could not always afford to eat. It takes a particular kind of person to emerge from that and conclude that a nation's most undervalued asset sits not in its server farms but in the heads of its retiring machinists and nurses."Every generation should start where the last one left off," Inam says. It sounds like a product principle. It is closer to a family creed — the thing his father practised without ever calling it a thesis, the thing his mother recognised on a television screen in a language she does not speak. Some knowledge, it turns out, transfers just fine.
Article Summary: Ahmer Inam, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it. The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage" By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030.

Article Title: Apple releases macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 to fix Screen Sharing security flaw
Article Text:
Mac users can check for the latest update in the Settings app

How to download macOS Tahoe 26.6.1

Apple's most popular Mac is now its hardest to buy

Apple has released macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, a new security update for Mac users that fixes a vulnerability related to the Screen Sharing feature. According to Apple’s security support document, the flaw could allow an attacker to authenticate to Screen Sharing without having valid credentials. Apple says it has addressed the security issue by improving state management. The company has also released updates for older macOS versions, including macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, with the same security fix.The fix is not limited to Macs running macOS Tahoe. Apple has also released macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, which address the same Screen Sharing vulnerability. This means Mac users who have not upgraded to macOS Tahoe can also install the security fix while remaining on their existing supported macOS version.Mac users can check for the latest update by opening the System Settings app and navigating to the Software Update section. If macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 is available for the device, users can download and install it from there.Given that the update addresses a security vulnerability that could allow authentication without valid credentials, users may want to install the latest available update on their Macs.In another news, shipping estimates of Apple MacBook Air have slipped by weeks across nearly every configuration, likely because of the global memory shortage. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in his Power On newsletter that retail sources describe Air inventory as more constrained than they can ever recall. Order a base model from Apple's online store today and delivery lands at the end of August. Buyers of the Apple MacBook Air are reportedly being told to wait till early September to get hold of the device.
Article Summary: macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 is a new security update for Mac users that fixes a vulnerability related to the Screen Sharing feature. The flaw could allow an attacker to authenticate to Screen Sharing without having valid credentials. Apple has also released updates for older macOS versions, including macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9.

Native Hindi language support

Article Title: Hacked AI email accounts can help attackers steal $250,000 through CEO fraud: Report
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

How the attack unfolded

AI helped attackers compromise the CEO

Attackers also concealed the fraud

AI increases the speed of post-compromise attacks

Hacked artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled email accounts can accelerate cyberattacks. A new report from Barracuda's Red Team says attackers who gain access to AI-enabled business email accounts can use built-in AI assistants to identify sensitive information, impersonate executives and redirect payments. In a controlled proof-of-concept, researchers demonstrated how a compromised employee account could escalate into CEO fraud and lead to the theft of $247,500 (nearly $250,000) through a fraudulent wire transfer.The report says the risk does not stem from AI creating new privileges, but from helping attackers use the permissions they already have more quickly. By leveraging AI assistants such as Microsoft Copilot, attackers were able to automate reconnaissance, draft convincing phishing emails, establish persistence inside compromised accounts and carry out business email compromise (BEC) attacks.According to Barracuda, the simulated attack began after an attacker gained access to an employee's AI-enabled email account. Using the built-in AI assistant, the attacker first created inbox rules that automatically moved login notifications to the Deleted Items folder, reducing the victim's chances of detecting suspicious sign-ins.The AI assistant was then used to analyse emails, documents, calendar entries and organisational relationships to identify senior executives inside the company.Researchers said the compromised AI assistant also drafted a phishing email in the employee's writing style, which was sent to the CEO from the employee's legitimate mailbox.After the CEO clicked the phishing link, the attacker used an adversary-in-the-middle attack to steal the CEO's authenticated session token, granting access to the CEO's account and bypassing multi-factor authentication.The attackers then repeated the inbox rule tactic to suppress security notifications in the CEO's mailbox before using the AI assistant to summarise recent financial conversations.According to the report, a prompt requesting recent invoices, payment amounts, and upcoming transfers quickly surfaced a pending $247,500 wire transfer awaiting final approval.The AI assistant was then used to draft an email from the CEO's account requesting that the finance team update the recipient's bank account details before processing the payment.Because the message originated from the CEO's genuine mailbox, matched the executive's writing style and referenced an active transaction, the finance team updated the banking information and transferred the funds to an attacker-controlled account as part of the simulation.To prevent the CEO from seeing confirmation emails, the attackers created another inbox rule that automatically forwarded messages from the finance team to an attacker-controlled email address while hiding them from the CEO's inbox.The report also showed how the AI assistant could quickly identify emails related to the fraudulent transaction, allowing attackers to remove evidence more efficiently than through manual searches.Barracuda said the proof of concept demonstrates that AI assistants do not introduce new access rights but significantly increase the speed and scale at which attackers can exploit compromised accounts."The primary security risk posed by AI assistants is not that they create new privileges, but that they dramatically increase the speed, scale and effectiveness with which attackers can exploit the privileges they already obtain through account compromise," the report said.The company added that organisations should focus on preventing the initial account compromise while monitoring AI-enabled accounts for suspicious activity such as inbox rule abuse, persistence mechanisms and business email compromise attempts.According to Barracuda, securing AI-enabled email accounts should become a core part of enterprise identity and email security strategies as AI assistants become more widely integrated into workplace communication and business workflows.
Article Summary: Attackers can use built-in AI assistants to identify sensitive information, impersonate executives and redirect payments. Researchers demonstrated how a compromised employee account could escalate into CEO fraud and lead to the theft of $247,500 (nearly $250,000) through a fraudulent wire transfer.

Article Title: Spotify launches Premium Rewards in India, adds brand offers and invite-only events for subscribers
Article Text:
What's on offer



How subscribers can access it



Spotify has rolled out Premium Rewards in India, a new limited-edition initiative that gives Premium subscribers access to curated brand offers and invite-only live experiences, the company announced on Wednesday. The move adds a lifestyle and events layer on top of the music streaming service's existing offering of high-quality, ad-free, offline listening.Premium Rewards is built around two categories of benefits. The first is lifestyle perks — exclusive offers from partner brands including MakeMyTrip, Tira, Nykaa, Ajio Luxe, Gully Labs and Airbnb, spanning travel, beauty, fashion and lifestyle categories. The second is what Spotify is calling "IRL experiences": invite-only events, intimate listening sessions and cultural moments designed to give subscribers closer access to artists and music.Spotify says the rewards are curated around how subscribers actually live, travel and shop, positioning the initiative less as a set of discount coupons and more as an extension of the value of being a Premium member.Premium Rewards is available through a dedicated microsite, premiumrewards.byspotify.com, where Premium subscribers can browse available rewards and claim offers directly. Spotify says new perks and experiences will be added to the platform on an ongoing basis, suggesting the current lineup of brand partners and events is a starting point rather than a fixed list.The rewards program is live now and available to all Spotify Premium subscribers in India, with no separate sign-up or additional cost beyond an active Premium subscription.Shipra Srivastava, Head of Marketing at Spotify India, framed the launch as an attempt to extend Premium's value beyond the app itself. She said Premium has always centered on delivering the best audio experience — high quality, uninterrupted listening with offline access — and that Premium Rewards is meant to carry that same feeling into subscribers' everyday lives, the brands they engage with and the experiences they remember. She described the goal as making Premium function more like a membership than a plain subscription, adding that the rewards are being offered as a limited-edition experience for now, making the present moment a particularly good time to be a Premium subscriber in India.
Article Summary: Spotify has rolled out Premium Rewards in India. The initiative gives Premium subscribers access to curated brand offers and invite-only live experiences. The rewards are curated around how subscribers actually live, travel and shop. The move adds a lifestyle and events layer on top of the music streaming service's existing offering of ad-free, offline listening.

Article Title: Waymo co-CEO explains why physical AI can't follow Silicon Valley's 'move fast and break things' mantra
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

"

move fast and break things

"

"move fast and ship safely,"

"In Silicon Valley, there's a common mantra to 'move fast and break things.' However, when you're dealing with atoms instead of bits, breaking things is not really okay,”

'There's simply not an undo and a retry button': Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov on AI safety

"So the thing you have to do is to move fast and ship safely,”

"You have to build AI models, and you have to build training recipes where safety is the foundation and not an afterthought, not an add-on,”

"There's simply not an undo and a retry button."

Waymo co-CEO’s comments come amid AI safety concerns

Waymo has also faced regulatory scrutiny

Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov believes physical artificial intelligence (AI) requires safety-first development. He said AI used in the physical world cannot follow Silicon Valley's long-standingphilosophy because mistakes can have real-world consequences. Speaking during a Y Combinator talk released this week, Dolgov said developers building self-driving cars and robotics must insteadwith safety built into AI systems from the start.Dolgov said the difference between digital AI and physical AI lies in the cost of errors. While a mistake made by a chatbot may require only another prompt, failures involving autonomous vehicles or robots can put people at risk.Dolgov said.Dolgov, who has worked on Google's self-driving car project since 2009 and became part of Waymo after it was spun out as an Alphabet company in 2016, said physical AI systems must be designed with robustness and safety as core requirements rather than post-launch additions.he saidDolgov added.Explaining the distinction between generative AI and autonomous systems, he said, "You have a language model or a chatbot or a co-pilot, and it makes a mistake, usually it costs you a retry. In the physical world, the cost of a mistake can be measured in human lives, not tokens."He continued,Dolgov's remarks come as recent AI-related security incidents have renewed discussions around AI safety and oversight. Last month, Hugging Face disclosed a security breach in which an AI agent accessed some of its internal datasets. Around the same time, OpenAI said its models escaped a sandbox environment, accessed the internet and carried out a rogue hack.More recently, Anthropic reported a similar incident, saying it had identified cases in which Claude models gained unauthorised access to internal systems at three different companies.Reacting to the OpenAI incident, Box CEO Aaron Levie wrote on X: "If you were wondering how powerful AI is getting, Agents are now capable of escaping out of systems, finding their way to the internet, discovering zero day security vulnerabilities along the way, and then breaking into external systems - all in an attempt to complete their goal."Waymo has logged millions of autonomous driving miles while largely avoiding major injury-causing crashes, but the company has faced regulatory reviews over software-related issues.In 2024, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) opened an investigation into reports of unexpected driving behaviour, including collisions with stationary objects and traffic-law violations, which led to software recalls. In 2025 and earlier this year, Waymo also issued recalls after several robotaxis entered freeway construction zones.
Article Summary: Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov believes physical AI requires safety-first development. He said AI used in the physical world cannot follow Silicon Valley's long-standingphilosophy because mistakes can have real-world consequences. Dolgov's remarks come as recent AI-related security incidents have renewed discussions around AI safety.

Article Title: 'This person wasn't real': Arena CEO says AI job applicants fooled engineers during interviews
Article Text:

Company considering in-person onboarding

"People are trying to get into all of the American businesses.

We're not the only ones. This is happening everywhere."

AI-powered interview fraud has drawn attention from US authorities

How companies are tightening hiring verification

Arena has revealed that some candidates it interviewed were AI-generated rather than real people. Anastasios Angelopoulos, the co-founder and CEO of the AI model evaluation company, said that he encountered fake candidates that successfully cleared technical interviews before disappearing during the hiring process. Describing one such case, he said,adding that the incident has prompted the company to consider requiring in-person onboarding for new employees.Speaking on the "20VC" podcast released this week, Angelopoulos said Arena's engineers interviewed the candidates believing they were genuine applicants. He did not explain how the company later determined the applicants were AI-generated but said the incidents have raised concerns about identity verification during recruitment.he said.Angelopoulos said the experience is pushing Arena to rethink parts of its hiring process, particularly for remote employees. He said,He added that Arena is not alone in facing the issue. Angelopoulos noted,While Angelopoulos said he does not know who was behind the applications, he suggested possible motives could include corporate espionage, cyberattacks or attempts to gain access to company systems and source code.The comments come as US companies continue to face cases involving fake job applicants. In a 2025 alert, the FBI warned that North Korean IT workers were using AI and face-swapping technology during video interviews to conceal their identities and obtain remote jobs at US companies. According to the bureau, some of those workers later used their access to steal proprietary and sensitive information after securing employment at more than 100 US companies.The FBI advised employers to verify candidates' identities during interviews and onboarding (preferably in person) and to continue identity checks throughout remote employment.Several technology companies have introduced additional safeguards against fraudulent job applications. Coinbase now requires employees to attend in-person orientation in the US, while Amazon has used AI systems to identify and block applications suspected to be linked to North Korean operatives.Research firm Gartner also highlighted the growing issue in a second-quarter 2025 survey of 3,000 job candidates, which found that 6% admitted participating in interview fraud by either impersonating another person or having someone else attend an interview on their behalf.Gartner projects that one in four candidate profiles worldwide could be fake by 2028, underscoring the increasing challenge companies face in verifying applicants during remote hiring processes.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Larry Page: “You need to get one thing done well, or else…” - a reminder to stop chasing everything at once
Article Text:
Larry Page advocates for completing one task well before starting others. This focused approach builds confidence and a strong foundation for future endeavors. Many fields, including education and business, benefit from this principle of deep mastery. Rushing tasks can create future problems, while high standards require patience and revision. This principle remains relevant amidst modern distractions and constant communication shifts.

Quote of the day by Larry Page

“You need to get one thing done well, or else you don't have permission to do anything else.”

Understand the meaning behind Page’s quote

Why doing it well matters more than doing it quickly

All about Larry Page

Lessons that can be applied

Other famous quotes by Larry Page

“You never lose a dream, it just incubates as a hobby.”

“Always deliver more than expected.”

“When you aim for the stars you may come up short, but still reach the moon.”

“Have a healthy disregard for the impossible.”

Why the quote still feels relevant

With many distractions in this era and multitasking becoming the order of the day, staying focused has become one of the greatest struggles of the current generation. Larry Page, one of the co-founders of Google, is known to emphasise the need to combine ambition and execution well. This strategy is based on the notion that success only results when one identifies the appropriate priorities and pays adequate attention to accomplishing them. In education, in business, and in any area of creativity, distributing one’s attention to many things at once makes the process less efficient and sometimes the outcome less effective. Concentrating on fewer meaningful goals often improves decision-making, reduces unnecessary distractions and increases the likelihood of producing consistently high-quality results over time.Larry Page is pointing towards focus rather than limitation. Many people are tempted to divide their attention across several goals at once, believing that more activity automatically means greater achievement. The quote argues for almost the opposite approach.Completing one important objective creates a solid foundation.It develops confidence, demonstrates capability and often provides resources or knowledge that make the next challenge easier. Skipping this step can leave every project competing for time without any reaching a meaningful finish.This way of thinking appears in many fields. A student may benefit more from mastering one difficult subject before taking on several advanced courses. A business may be wiser to perfect one product before introducing five new ones. Even creative work often improves when attention is concentrated instead of scattered.There is another layer to the quote that is easy to miss. It is not simply about finishing something; it is about finishing it well.That distinction matters. Speed has obvious advantages, but rushing through an important task can create problems that demand even more attention later. High standards usually require patience, repeated revision and the willingness to ignore distractions.The quote also questions the appeal of constant expansion. Modern work often rewards visible activity. Meetings multiply, ideas accumulate and side projects appear before earlier ones are complete. Page's observation suggests that growth without a dependable foundation can become difficult to sustain.Larry Page is an American computer scientist and entrepreneur best known as the co-founder of Google alongside Sergey Brin. While both were doctoral students at Stanford University in the late 1990s, they developed a search engine that ranked web pages according to the relationships between links rather than simply counting keywords. That idea eventually became Google.As the company expanded, Page held several leadership roles, including chief executive. Under his leadership, Google broadened far beyond internet search into products and services covering advertising, mobile software, cloud computing and artificial intelligence. In 2015, Google became part of Alphabet, a new parent company created to oversee Google's operations alongside a range of long-term technology ventures.Throughout his career, Page has often spoken about ambitious thinking, engineering discipline and solving problems at large scale. Even so, many of his comments return to a familiar principle: meaningful progress usually begins with getting the fundamentals right.The quote lends itself to practical situations without requiring dramatic changes in behaviour.For professionals, it can mean identifying the task that has the greatest impact and giving it full attention before accepting additional responsibilities. Delivering reliable work often creates more opportunities than attempting everything at once.Students may see the same pattern in revision. Understanding one topic thoroughly can be more valuable than quickly reading several chapters without retaining much of the material.Business leaders can interpret the message as a reminder to strengthen existing operations before expanding into unfamiliar markets. Growth built on dependable systems tends to be easier to manage than growth driven only by enthusiasm.Creative people face similar choices. Whether writing, designing or developing software, completing one strong piece of work often provides a better platform than collecting unfinished ideas.The pace of modern communication encourages constant switching between priorities. Emails, messages and notifications compete for attention throughout the day, making uninterrupted work increasingly uncommon.Against that background, Page's words remain striking because they favour concentration over constant movement. The advice does not reject ambition. Instead, it asks whether ambition has been supported by consistent execution.Many organisations still rely on this principle when launching products. A reliable service with a clear purpose often earns trust more effectively than a broad collection of features that remain incomplete.
Article Summary: Larry Page is one of the co-founders of Google. He is known to emphasise the need to combine ambition and execution well. This focused approach builds confidence and a strong foundation for future endeavors. Rushing tasks can create future problems, while high standards require patience and revision.

Article Title: Redmi Note 17 with 8000 mAh battery , 50MP camera launched in India: Price, specs and more
Article Text:
Redmi Note 17: Price and availability

Variant MRP Introductory Price* 6GB + 128GB Rs 27,999 Rs 24,999 8GB + 128GB Rs 30,999 Rs 27,999

Redmi Note 17 specifications

Redmi Note 17 is here. Xiaomi has expanded its product lineup with the launch of Redmi Note 17 in India. The smartphone features a TrueColour AMOLED display and is backed by an 8,000 mAh battery. The smartphone packs Qualcomm Snapdragon chipset and houses a 50MP main camera. The Redmi Note 17 retains a slim and lightweight design while offering enhanced durability through Corning Gorilla Glass 7i, an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, a reinforced chassis, and HydroTouch 2.0 for reliable usability in everyday conditions.The Redmi Note 17 will be available in Dark Night, Arctic Blue, and Starlight Purple in two storage variants:Introductory prices include an instant bank discount of Rs 3,000 on SBI Card, Axis Bank, and Kotak Bank credit cards and EMI transactions.Customers will also receive 5TB of JioAI Cloud storage with Jio True 5G, 3 months of YouTube Premium Lite, and 6 months of Google One (200GB cloud storage).The REDMI Note 17 will be available starting 12:00 PM IST on 13th August 2026 via mi.com , Amazon Specials, and Xiaomi Retail.The Redmi Note 17 sports a 6.99-inch FHD+ OLED display with a resolution of 2396×1080 pixels, offering a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, 240Hz touch sampling rate, and up to 1800 nits peak brightness for vivid visuals.The screen is protected by Corning Gorilla Glass 7i, ensuring resilience against scratches and minor drops. Under the hood, it runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 4nm SoC, featuring an octa-core CPU with two Cortex-A78 cores clocked at 2.3GHz and six Cortex-A55 cores at 2GHz, paired with an Adreno 613 GPU for efficient graphics performance. Memory options include 6GB or 8GB LPDDR4X RAM with 128GB UFS 2.2 internal storage, expandable via microSD.The device operates on Android 16 with Xiaomi’s Hyper OS 3, offering a refined software experience. Camera capabilities include a 50MP main sensor with f/1.8 aperture and LED flash, capable of recording up to 1080p video, alongside an 8MP front camera with f/2.0 aperture for selfies and video calls. Security and convenience are enhanced with an in-display fingerprint sensor and infrared sensor. Audio is delivered through a bottom-ported speaker, while IP65 certification ensures dust and splash resistance.Connectivity options are comprehensive, with support for 5G, Dual 4G VoLTE, Wi-Fi 6 (2.4GHz + 5GHz), Bluetooth 5.1, GPS + GLONASS, and USB Type-C. Measuring 169.7×79.14×8.45mm and weighing 225g, the phone balances size with portability. Powering the device is a robust 8000mAh battery, supporting 45W fast charging and 22.5W reverse wired charging, making it suitable for heavy users who need long-lasting performance.
Article Summary: Xiaomi has expanded its product lineup with the launch of Redmi Note 17 in India. The smartphone features a TrueColour AMOLED display and is backed by an 8,000 mAh battery. The phone will be available in Dark Night, Arctic Blue, and Starlight Purple in two storage variants.
